speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you've experienced any recent headaches, stiff neck, or sensitivity to light along with your fever and confusion? Also, have you had any recent travel, mosquito bites, or contact with sick individuals?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, are you experiencing any muscle stiffness, tremors, or difficulty swallowing? Also, has anyone noticed any changes in your breathing or heart rate recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have profuse sweating, generalized rigidity, and altered mentation while on haloperidol, which is highly concerning for Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I will now request an immediate Creatine Kinase (CK) level and a complete blood count to confirm this. REQUEST TEST: Creatine Kinase. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: White Blood Cell Count: 14,700/mm3 (elevated); Creatine Kinase: 5600 U/L (elevated).

speaker: Doctor
text: Your elevated white blood cell count and significantly high creatine kinase levels, combined with your fever, rigidity, and confusion while on haloperidol, confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
